label: Aiyotsu
notes: Same-sided stance relationship, such as right-versus-right or left-versus-left.

label: Kenkayotsu
notes: Opposite-sided stance relationship, such as right-versus-left.

label: Georgian grip
notes: Over-the-back or belt-control gripping family. Competition use can depend on attack timing and ruleset context.

label: Leg control
notes: Hand or arm control below the belt, including classic leg-grab entries. IJF legality must be checked separately.

label: Mount
notes: Top position with tori straddling uke. In judo this overlaps with tate-shiho-gatame contexts; in BJJ it is a primary control position.

label: North-south
notes: Top-to-head orientation over uke. In judo this overlaps with kami-shiho-gatame and kuzure-kami-shiho-gatame contexts.

label: Guard
notes: Ground position where the bottom player uses the legs to control distance, posture, or attacking angles.

label: Collar-sleeve control
notes: Gi grip family controlling uke with one collar grip and one sleeve grip. From guard this is commonly called collar-sleeve guard; same-side and cross-side versions should be modeled as variants when needed.

label: Side control
notes: Cross-body top control orientation. In judo this overlaps with yoko-shiho-gatame and related hold-down contexts.

label: Frame control
notes: Defensive structure using forearms, hands, knees, or shins to manage distance and create escape space.

label: Underhook / hip control
notes: Ground escape control built from an underhook, far-hip, belt, or waist connection used to turn in, come up, or recover guard.

label: Over-back / belt control
notes: Georgian-grip-adjacent ground control using over-back, belt, or far-side waist connection during escapes or reversals.
